note: Re-confirmed 2026-09-08 after the functional-design redo jump, and re-saved following that confirmation. Coverage unchanged.

coverage.target: BR4.3 — AC owned by u4-owner-shell; enforced here by keeping each FieldError bound to its named field rather than flattening details into one message, which is what lets the signup form render an error beside the input that caused it

BR4.1, BR4.3 — AC owned by u4-owner-shell; enforced here by returning one typed UNAUTHORIZED for both a wrong password and an unknown username, so the shell has no way to distinguish them and cannot disclose which. BR4.3's note records login as the one deliberate exception to per-field details

BR1.4, and functional-spec.md > State machine > 'App loads with tokens in the store' — this unit's half is designed: tokens persist and the session is restored before any route guard runs. The criterion cannot be met end to end until AC4.1.4, because GET /v1/accounts/me does not exist and there is no other way to resolve the current account from a stored token. Recorded as Deferred rather than OK: the story map names this block explicitly

BR3.2 — AC owned by u5-owner-guide; enforced here by refusing to send a guide save that does not carry the complete section set under the exact key, since the route returns 200 with everything deleted rather than an error
BR3.5 — AC owned by u5-owner-guide; enforced here by disabling refetch-on-focus and prefetch as client configuration, since the guide GET creates an empty draft row as a side effect

BR1.3, and functional-spec.md > State machine > the two non-signed-out endedReason rows — AC owned by u4-owner-shell; this unit produces an explicit ended session with a reason rather than a silent failure, which is what lets the shell render an expiry state instead of a generic error
BR1.5 — AC owned by u4-owner-shell; every terminal path clears local session state and the token store
BR1.5, BR2.2 — AC owned by u5-owner-guide; BR1.5 guarantees session teardown does not touch caller state, so the editor's buffer survives, and BR2.2 governs what happens to the failed save afterwards

BR1.2, and functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 3 — AC owned by u4-owner-shell; exactly one RefreshFlight exists and every other request parks on its result. See BR1.6 for the cross-tab limit this does not cover
BR1.3, and functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 5b — AC owned by u4-owner-shell; a 401 from the refresh call itself ends the session and never starts another flight

BR1.5 covers the second half — local session state is cleared. The first half, server-side revocation, cannot be built: there is no logout or revocation endpoint anywhere in the API, and the refresh token is valid for seven days regardless. Blocked on AC4.1.5; until it lands, logout is a client-side discard that leaves a valid refresh token in existence

BR3.1 — AC owned by u6-owner-locality-billing; enforced here by refusing to send any request without a complete body, since the favourites handler destructures request.body with no fallback and returns 500 rather than 400

BR2.3, BR3.4, BR3.6 — AC owned by u6-owner-locality-billing. BR3.4 makes no-automatic-retry the default for every non-idempotent write after an indeterminate failure; BR2.3 excludes PATCH /v1/subscriptions from the Q2 = B replay path, since a session that ended mid-request is indeterminate; BR3.6 records the one case that is NOT indeterminate — a post-refresh retry, where auth runs as a preHandler so the request provably did not execute — and requires the outgoing guards to re-run on it

BR3.3 — AC owned by u6-owner-locality-billing; enforced here by a runtime check that the action is one of upgrade, downgrade or cancel before the request leaves, since the endpoint's final else branch cancels on anything unrecognised

BR5.2, and functional-spec.md > Workflow 4 step 3 — AC owned by u8-guest-app; a brand carrying only a name and tagline resolves to base tokens plus that name, so there is no partial set for a component to half-render

BR4.1, BR4.2 — AC owned by u8-guest-app; nothing above this unit ever sees an HTTP status, so no raw code can reach the screen, and the total union means an infrastructure failure resolves to a message rather than an unhandled parse error
BR4.2 — AC owned by u8-guest-app; TRANSPORT_FAILURE gives a failed load a defined error to render with a retry, including the non-envelope cases the backend is documented to produce
BR4.4 — AC owned by u8-guest-app; RATE_LIMITED is its own code and is never collapsed into a generic error, which is what lets the guest see a specific too-many-requests state

reverse.target: the no-raw-token rule. It traces to NFR7 rather than to any acceptance criterion, because it describes an absence — there is no token field on Session for a criterion to assert against. Structurally enforced: only SessionManager can name the TokenStore port (entities.md)

the reload-survival rule. Its only acceptance criterion, AC1.3.3, is itself Deferred on AC4.1.4 — the design is complete on this side of the boundary and the criterion cannot be demonstrated until GET /v1/accounts/me exists. Recorded here rather than left to derive as an orphan, because the rule is real and built, not absent

a constraint on OQ3's answer rather than a behaviour this stage builds. AC1.10.4 asserts single-flight within a document; the cross-tab race has no criterion because US1.10's own note recorded it as unspecifiable while OQ3 was open. Q1 = A makes it real, so it is stated here as a requirement flowing to nfr-design (rules.md > BR1.6 note)

loop prevention on the post-refresh retry. No acceptance criterion covers it: AC1.10.5 covers a 401 from the refresh CALL, which is a different event, and the retry case had no rule at all until review found the state machine would have routed it back into a second RefreshFlight. Specified in functional-spec.md > State machine > the post-refresh-retry row, and Workflow 1 step 7

transparent re-issue of reads after re-authentication. No criterion covers it because nothing user-visible happens — that is the point of the rule. Specified in functional-spec.md > Workflow 2 step 6 and its classification table

the single-parse and cannot-throw rule for visualStyling. Traces to the team's untrusted-render practice and Contract Design C3, not to a story: its effect is that no component can reach the raw blob, which is structural. Its failure mode — a parse throwing on hostile input — would surface as AC2.5.2's failed load, asserted there

the contrast-floor replacement. Traces to NFR3, which is a per-brand runtime property with no story-level criterion. Specified in functional-spec.md > Workflow 4 step 5; the gap that nothing reports a degraded brand is named in the rule's own note and belongs to nfr-design

branding on the guest invalid-link path. It has no acceptance criterion because US2.2 recorded it as open question OQ2 and ADR-005 decided it at domain design instead. Blocked on AC4.1.7 regardless — a 410 carries no payload to resolve a brand from, and the brand read currently requires a session
